body.statement: For the exact late-ramp pair and every possibly randomized confidence set \(D_n\) measurable from \(O_n\), if \(\liminf_n\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}\Pr_{\sigma}(\tau_n^{\sigma}\in D_n)\ge0.95\), then for each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), \(\liminf_n\Pr_{\sigma}(\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge1/8)\ge\sqrt{1/2}-0.1=0.6071067811865475\ldots\).
body.justification: The theorem establishes an information bound for every honest confidence set from the complete logged experiment, not an estimator-specific implication of the HT limit.
body.gap: ShekharRamdas2023 treats i.i.d. bounded-mean width and HongLeungLi2020 treats diverging effective information; neither uses a shared adaptive void event with this exact finite-population constant.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a quantitative warning that nominally valid inference cannot be uniformly narrow when an arm receives only bounded cumulative allocation hazard.
